name: SISTEr
aliases: Stress Incontinence Surgical Treatment Efficacy Trial
question: Does an autologous rectus fascial pubovaginal sling improve continence over Burch colposuspension in women with stress-predominant urinary incontinence?

design.population: Women with pure or stress-predominant urinary incontinence, a positive stress test and urethral hypermobility; prior incontinence surgery was permitted.
design.description: Nine-center randomized surgical superiority trial with 24-month time-to-event analysis

verdictNote: Both prespecified success composites favored sling; urinary infections and emptying problems were more frequent.
takeaway: In women with stress-predominant incontinence and urethral hypermobility, autologous rectus fascial pubovaginal sling improved 24-month overall and stress-specific success over Burch colposuspension (47% versus 38%; 66% versus 49%), with more urinary tract infections and voiding dysfunction.

reports.label: Two-year randomized report
reports.citation: Albo ME, Richter HE, Brubaker L, et al. Burch colposuspension versus fascial sling to reduce urinary stress incontinence. *N Engl J Med.* 2007;356(21):2143-2155. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa070416
reports.followUp: 24 months; 520/655 women had an assessed outcome or a prior documented failure
reports.followUpLocator: NEJM PDF p5, Figure 2; journal p2147

results.measure: 24-month Kaplan–Meier overall composite success; absolute risk difference in percentage points (sling minus Burch)
results.note: Time-to-event estimates, not numerators divided by randomized group sizes. Composite required no symptoms, pad gain <15 g, no diary leakage, negative stress test and no retreatment.
results.locator: NEJM PDF pp5,10, Figure 3A; journal pp2147,2152

results.measure: 24-month Kaplan–Meier stress-specific composite success; absolute risk difference in percentage points (sling minus Burch)
results.note: Required no self-reported stress symptoms, negative stress test and no retreatment for stress incontinence.
results.locator: NEJM PDF pp5,10, Figure 3B; journal pp2147,2152

harms.label: Any adverse event
harms.locator: NEJM PDF pp5,9, Table 2; journal pp2147,2151
harms.note: 415 versus 305 total events; the excess was primarily urinary infection.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.note: Cystitis could be culture-proven or treated on clinical suspicion; 305 versus 203 genitourinary adverse-event episodes were recorded.

harms.label: Voiding dysfunction after six weeks
harms.note: Defined as catheter use after six weeks or a revision to improve emptying. Nineteen sling recipients had 20 revision procedures; no Burch recipient had one.

harms.label: Treated postoperative urge incontinence
harms.note: Persistent treated urge incontinence: 79/326 (24%) versus 59/329 (18%); new treated cases: 11/326 (3%) versus 11/329 (3%).

harms.label: Serious adverse event (modified Dindo grade III–V)
harms.locator: NEJM PDF p8, Table 2; journal p2150
harms.note: P=0.20; no grade V events. Incident cystotomy: 2 sling versus 10 Burch; ureteral injuries: 0 versus 2.

delivery.label: Assigned operations performed
delivery.locator: NEJM PDF p5, Figure 2; journal p2147
delivery.note: Randomization occurred in the operating room after induction of anesthesia.

delivery.label: Concomitant prolapse surgery
delivery.note: Planned procedures were declared before randomization; abdominal and vaginal repairs and hysterectomy were allowed.

reports.label: Preoperative urodynamic predictors
reports.citation: Nager CW, FitzGerald M, Kraus SR, et al. Urodynamic measures do not predict stress continence outcomes after surgery for stress urinary incontinence in selected women. *J Urol.* 2008;179(4):1470-1474. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2007.11.077
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract; primary NEJM PDF pp4–5

results.endpoint: Preoperative urodynamic predictors of overall success
results.measure: Odds ratio for overall success with versus without urodynamic stress incontinence, pooled across operations
results.note: The trend did not reach statistical significance; Valsalva leak point pressure and detrusor overactivity did not predict success.

reports.label: E-SISTEr five-year observational follow-up
reports.citation: Brubaker L, Richter HE, Norton PA, et al. 5-year continence rates, satisfaction and adverse events of Burch urethropexy and fascial sling surgery for urinary incontinence. *J Urol.* 2012;187(4):1324-1330. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2011.11.087
reports.followUp: Annual assessment through at least five postoperative years; 482/655 entered the extension

results.measure: Five-year Kaplan–Meier continence under the extension composite
results.note: Extension composite required no diary leakage, no self-reported stress symptoms and no stress-incontinence surgical retreatment; incontinent trial participants enrolled more often.
Respondent percentages, not cumulative continence estimates.

harms.label: Adverse events during long-term extension
harms.note: Reported among the extension groups: sling n=243, Burch n=239; percentages are the article's rounded values.

delivery.label: Enrolled in E-SISTEr
delivery.note: Participants with incontinence at two years enrolled more often (85.5% versus 52.2%).
